Suppose that $L$ is the line in $\real^3$ defined by the vector $\wvec=\threevec{1}{2}{-2}$.

Find an orthonormal basis $\uvec$ for $L$.

Construct the matrix $Q = \begin{bmatrix}\uvec\end{bmatrix}$ and use it to construct the matrix $P$ that projects vectors orthogonally onto $L$.

Use your matrix to find $\bhat$, the orthogonal projection of $\bvec=\threevec111$ onto $L$.

Find $\rank(P)$ and explain its geometric significance.

The vectors $$ \wvec_1 = \fourvec1111,\hspace{24pt} \wvec_2 = \fourvec011{-2} $$ form an orthogonal basis of $W$, a two-dimensional subspace of $\real^4$.

Use the projection formula from [prop-proj-formula] to find $\bhat$, the orthogonal projection of $\bvec=\fourvec92{-2}3$ onto $W$.

Find an orthonormal basis $\uvec_1$ and $\uvec_2$ for $W$ and use it to construct the matrix $P$ that projects vectors orthogonally onto $W$. Check that $P\bvec = \bhat$, the orthogonal projection you found in the previous part of this activity.

Find $\rank(P)$ and explain its geometric significance.

Find a basis for $W^\perp$.

Find a vector $\bvec^\perp$ in $W^\perp$ such that $$ \bvec = \bhat + \bvec^\perp. $$

If $Q$ is the matrix whose columns are $\uvec_1$ and $\uvec_2$, find the product $Q^TQ$ and explain your result.
